# Churchill Downs News Updates: Gramp's Legacy Goes Gate to Wire in $300,000 Commonwealth Turf


## Nov 21, 2026


Gramp’s Legacy rationed his early speed and led every step of the way to win the 21st running of the $300,000 Commonwealth Turf (Grade III) by one length over odds-on 3-5 favorite Remember Mamba on Saturday at Churchill Downs.


Gramp’s Legacy ran 1 1/16 miles over “firm” turf in 1:42.85. Johan Rosado rode the winner for trainer Jerry O’Dwyer and owner/breeder Tyler Sliney.


This was Gramp’s Legacy’s first try against stakes company after three consecutive grass wins at Colonial Downs. Additionally, it was the first graded stakes win for Rosado.


Breaking from post No. 2, Gramp’s Legacy asserted himself to the front in a field of seven 3-year-olds devoid of early speed through tepid and unpressured fractions of :24.26, :50.45 and 1:15.35. Sensing a slow pace while racing in fifth early on, Transylvania Stakes (GIII) winner Remember Mamba slipped through an opening along the rail to improve to third just before the half-mile pole. Into the final turn, Fuzzbuster got within a half-length of Gramp’s Legacy and Remember Mamba was urged to kick on, but Gramp’s Legacy had plenty of energy left for the stretch run. He opened his lead to two lengths in the stretch and continued on late for the stakes triumph under a jubilant Rosado.


“I just wanted to set easy fractions because I knew Remember Mamba would be coming,” Rosado said. “I kept him comfortable all the way around there and had plenty left down the lane.”


Gramp’s Legacy netted $151,900 and now boasts career earnings of $402,100 from a record of 5-1-1 in nine starts.


“We tried to run him in the Bryan Station (GII) at Keeneland but drew on the also-eligible list,” O’Dwyer said. “Even if we got in, we probably wouldn’t have run with the outside draw and the loose ground that day. The owners have been so great because they’ve been patient and let me to take my time and pick our right spots. It’s great all of that was rewarded today winning a Grade III at Churchill Downs.”


This was just the fourth graded stakes win of O’Dwyer’s training career. Previously, he won the 2019 Remsen (GII) with Shotski and the 2022-23 editions of the Mr. Prospector (GIII) with Silbelius.


Gramp’s Legacy returned $15.34, $5.58 and $3.78 as the 6-1 fourth betting choice. Remember Mamba, with Jose Ortiz up, paid $2.58 and $2.10. Fuzzbuster, ridden by Luis Saez at 7-2, paid $2.54 to show.


Royal Causeway, Winter Holiday, Banksy’s and Corona de Oro completed the order of finish. Beautiful War and No Joke Joe were scratched.


Gramp’s Legacy is a gelded son of Funtastic out of the Cactus Ridge mare Ridgester and was bred in Virginia by his owner.


The horse is named for his owner/breeder’s late father who, according to Sliney, had more than 40 grandchildren.
